statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-44740 (GHSA-m3xc-h892-ggx6, GO-2026-5490): in github.com/go-git/go-billy/v5 before 5.9.0, symlink resolution has no depth limit or cycle detection, so crafted filesystem content can cause infinite loops and resource exhaustion. It is fixed in v5.9.0 by https://github.com/go-git/go-billy/pull/203, merge commit https://github.com/go-git/go-billy/commit/427b27f32f22de11498a682c65cd5060a01ec168 on the releases/v5.x branch, which adds symlink-loop detection to helper/chroot: https://github.com/go-git/go-billy/security/advisories/GHSA-m3xc-h892-ggx6, https://github.com/go-git/go-billy/releases/tag/v5.9.0. The Go vulnerability database lists util.Walk and, in helper/chroot, New and ChrootHelper.Chroot as affected: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5490. We read every published trivy-dev package for Alpine 3.23 in the DHI Alpine repository: 38 builds, 0.69.1-r0 to the current 0.74.0-r12, each for x86_64 and aarch64, each verified against the checksum in the package index. Each package installs one file, /usr/bin/trivy, a Go program built with CGO_ENABLED=0 that keeps its symbol table; we read its Go build information, its function table (which lists runtime.main in every binary) and its raw bytes. Every build has the affected function (*ChrootHelper).Chroot in its function table. The build information lists go-billy v5.7.0 in 0.69.1-r0, v5.8.0 in 0.69.2-r0 to 0.70.0-r0, v5.9.0 in 0.70.0-r1 to 0.71.2-r3, v5.9.1 in 0.73.0-r0 to 0.74.0-r5 and v5.9.2 from 0.74.0-r6. The function table agrees: in 0.70.0-r0 the helper/chroot functions come from go-billy v5.8.0 source and include none of the functions the fix adds, and from 0.70.0-r1 they come from v5.9.0 or later and include (*ChrootHelper).followedPath, resolveFollowedPath and resolveFollowedRoot from the fix. The range is therefore fixed at 0.70.0-r1.
